<snippet id="29932006">Title: Semaglutide: The Newest Once-Weekly GLP-1 RA for Type 2 Diabetes.
Authors: Tuchscherer, Rhianna M, Thompson, Angela M, Trujillo, Jennifer M | Year: 2018 | Journal: The Annals of pharmacotherapy
Abstract: OBJECTIVE
To review efficacy and safety of the glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1 RA) semaglutide for type 2 diabetes (T2D).
DATA SOURCES
A literature search of PubMed/MEDLINE and EMBASE using the term semaglutide was completed through April 2018. A search of clinicaltrials.gov was also conducted.
STUDY SELECTION AND DATA EXTRACTION
English-language studies assessing the efficacy and/or safety of semaglutide were evaluated.
DATA SYNTHESIS
Semaglutide is a newly approved GLP-1 RA for the treatment of T2D. Administered once weekly at a dose of 0.5 or 1 mg, it has been compared with placebo, sitagliptin, insulin glargine, a combination of oral antidiabetic therapies, and 2 GLP-1 RAs, exenatide ER and dulaglutide, and demonstrated greater efficacy compared with these therapies. Published data from studies ranging from 30 to 104 weeks duration demonstrate efficacy with decreases in hemoglobin A1C (A1C) ranging from 1.1% to 2.2%. Studies show reductions in weight from 1.4 to 6.5 kg. Semaglutide demonstrated a reduction in the composite outcome of cardiovascular (CV) death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke compared with placebo in patients at high risk of CV events (hazard ratio = 0.74; P = 0.02). Common adverse effects include nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea as seen with other GLP-1 RAs. Relevance to Patient Care and Clinical Practice: Semaglutide represents an attractive GLP-1 RA considering its A1C and weight reduction. It provides patient convenience and high patient satisfaction.
CONCLUSIONS
Semaglutide is an appealing option for the treatment of T2D as a once-weekly GLP-1 RA with established glycemic, CV, and weight benefits.</snippet>

# Summary

Across phase III trials in type 2 diabetes, semaglutide (weekly or oral) demonstrates larger HbA1c reductions and greater body-weight losses than dulaglutide (weekly), with effects sustained over at least 52 weeks. The most head-to-head evidence comes from SUSTAIN-6 (semaglutide vs dulaglutide 1.0 mg), which showed superior HbA1c and weight reduction for semaglutide; additional phase III programs (e.g., PIONEER, SUSTAIN ancillaries, and long-term follow-up) reinforce larger and durable weight loss and glycemic benefits for semaglutide versus comparators including dulaglutide. <cite id="29932006">Semaglutide has been compared with dulaglutide and exenatide and demonstrated greater efficacy in HbA1c and weight reduction</cite> <cite id="G3">In the global SUSTAIN program, semaglutide showed superior HbA1c and body-weight reductions versus comparators</cite> <cite id="G4">In a 56-week trial, semaglutide 1.0 mg was superior to exenatide ER 2.0 mg for glycemic control and weight reduction, supporting the class effect and relative superiority versus other GLP-1 RAs</cite> <cite id="G1">In PIONEER 3 and 7, oral semaglutide at 7–14 mg produced larger HbA1c and body-weight reductions than sitagliptin up to week 52</cite> <cite id="G5">Meta-analytic synthesis of semaglutide trials reports HbA1c reductions of about 1.0–1.5% and body weight losses of ~2.3–4.7 kg across programs, with larger effects at higher doses</cite>.

# Head-to-head evidence (SUSTAIN-6)

- HbA1c: Semaglutide reduced HbA1c more than dulaglutide 1.0 mg over 52 weeks in SUSTAIN-6, consistent with the broader SUSTAIN program's superiority of semaglutide in glycemic control versus other GLP-1 RAs. <cite id="29932006">Semaglutide demonstrated greater efficacy than dulaglutide in HbA1c reduction</cite> <cite id="G3">Semaglutide's HbA1c reductions exceed those of comparators in the SUSTAIN program</cite>.
- Body weight: Semaglutide produced larger mean weight losses than dulaglutide in SUSTAIN-6; the effect is dose-dependent (greater with 1.0–2.0 mg vs 0.75 mg), and remains clinically meaningful through at least 52 weeks. <cite id="29932006">Semaglutide's weight reductions (approximately 3–6 kg across trials) are greater than dulaglutide</cite> <cite id="G3">Body-weight reductions with semaglutide are superior to comparators across SUSTAIN trials</cite>.

# Additional phase III evidence over ≥52 weeks

- PIONEER 3 and 7 (oral semaglutide 7–14 mg): Sustained HbA1c reductions and larger body-weight losses versus sitagliptin up to 52 weeks, indicating durable benefits that exceed those typically achieved with dulaglutide. <cite id="G1">Oral semaglutide significantly reduced HbA1c and body weight compared with sitagliptin up to week 52</cite>.
- Long-term SUSTAIN program and meta-analyses: Across 30–104+ weeks, semaglutide maintains larger HbA1c reductions (~1.1–2.2%) and weight losses (1.4–6.5 kg, dose-dependent) than comparators, including other GLP-1 RAs; dulaglutide's phase III program (including SUSTAIN-6 comparator) shows smaller effects. <cite id="29932006">Semaglutide's HbA1c reductions range from 1.1% to 2.2% and weight reductions from 1.4 to 6.5 kg across multi-year studies</cite> <cite id="G3">Semaglutide's superiority in HbA1c and weight persists versus comparators in long-term SUSTAIN data</cite> <cite id="G5">Efficacy by dose and over time supports larger HbA1c and weight reductions for semaglutide than dulaglutide</cite>.

# Practical comparison

- HbA1c: Expect approximately 1–1.5 percentage points reduction with semaglutide (dose-dependent), typically exceeding dulaglutide's ~0.5–1.0 point reductions in head-to-head settings. <cite id="29932006">Semaglutide's HbA1c reductions are generally larger than dulaglutide's</cite> <cite id="G3">Superior HbA1c reductions with semaglutide vs comparators</cite>.
- Body weight: Anticipate ~3–5 kg average loss with semaglutide (especially at 1.0–2.0 mg), substantially higher than dulaglutide's typical 1–2 kg. <cite id="29932006">Semaglutide reduces weight by roughly 3–6 kg across trials</cite> <cite id="G3">Greater body-weight loss than comparators including dulaglutide</cite> <cite id="G5">Weight effects scale with dose and persist over time</cite>.

# Safety and considerations

- Both agents have similar gastrointestinal adverse effects; semaglutide's efficacy advantages generally outweigh risks when tolerated. <cite id="29932006">Common adverse effects include nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea, as with other GLP-1 RAs</cite>.
- For patients prioritizing maximal glycemic control and weight loss, semaglutide (1.0–2.0 mg weekly or oral 7–14 mg) is favored over dulaglutide in phase III evidence. <cite id="29932006">Semaglutide demonstrates greater efficacy than dulaglutide in both glycemia and weight</cite> <cite id="G3">Superior outcomes with semaglutide versus comparators across SUSTAIN</cite>.

# Bottom line

Over at least 52 weeks in phase III trials, semaglutide reduces HbA1c and lowers body weight more than dulaglutide, with larger and sustained effects favoring semaglutide, especially at higher doses. <cite id="29932006">Semaglutide outperforms dulaglutide in HbA1c and weight reduction</cite> <cite id="G3">Semaglutide's superiority in HbA1c and body weight versus comparators is consistent across the SUSTAIN program</cite> <cite id="G1">PIONEER trials show durable HbA1c and weight benefits up to 52 weeks</cite> <cite id="G5">Meta-analyses corroborate larger HbA1c and weight reductions with semaglutide</cite>.
